body.body: I've retested with gt 1.1.0, which is the same commit as main (44915d2), and updated the description with its output. Both problems remain: `gt run view`, `gt run jobs` and `gt run logs` fail on the bare-array job listing, and run URLs from `gt pr checks` resolve to the wrong run. I also added the version message from `gt project workflow list`, which calls Forgejo 17.0.1 "Gitea 17.0.1".

Thanks for the detailed report and for retesting on 1.1.0.

We have to decline this one. Forgejo is a downstream fork that has made breaking changes to the API and the web URL scheme. This repo targets Gitea, and we can't track every divergence in a fork. That includes:

- the bare-array job listing
- run numbers instead of run IDs in web URLs
- the version string format

There is a second problem. Even if we adapted gt to Forgejo 17 today, we can't guarantee that Forgejo won't change these behaviors again later. Every such change would need a new Forgejo-specific fix, and we couldn't test or verify them against the fork. The workarounds would keep breaking, and the maintenance cost would fall on this repo. #56 was a narrow fallback for a missing endpoint, not a commitment to support Forgejo. We don't plan to extend it.

Forgejo users will have to rely on best-effort compatibility, and some commands may not work. A Forgejo-specific client, or a community fork of gt that tracks Forgejo's API, is the better place for this.

For your case, `gt api` still works for the endpoints you listed. For example, GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/jobs/{id}/logs returns the plain-text log.

Closing as out of scope. Thanks again for the thorough write-up.
If somebody (e.g., me 😸) volunteered to maintain Forgejo bugs, would it change your position?

> If somebody (e.g., me 😸) volunteered to maintain Forgejo bugs, would it change your position?

Thank you for volunteering your time for this project. I still recommend creating it as a fork.

Most users of `gt` are likely to use Gitea, so it’s unclear how many maintainers would continue supporting this work if you lose interest.

I’ve heard that the Forgejo community may reject AI-generated code. Since this repository was largely generated with AI, it may not receive official support unless the community changes its rules.

You may also run into API conflicts between the two forges. In some cases, you’ll have to choose one API over the other, which could make it difficult to support both.
